title: Admissibility under state mapping
statement: Let $M,N$ be machines, let $E$ map configurations of $M$ to configurations of $N$, and let $c\text{ost}$ assign a natural-number cost to each configuration of $M$. Let $C$ be a contract for $M$ with entry state $e$ and exit set $X$, and let $L$ be a lockstep relation between $M$ and $N$ using $E$, $c\text{ost}$, and exit sets $X,X'$. Let $\rho$ map states of $M$ to states of $N$, and suppose the state of $E(c)$ is obtained by applying $\rho$ to the optional state of every configuration $c$. Let $b_-,b_+$ assign integer bounds to each configuration of $M$ and tape of $N$, and assume that for every configuration $c$, every time $v$ that is zero or satisfies $c$'s state is outside $X$ and $v\le c\text{ost}(c)$, and every tape of $N$, the head position after $v$ steps from $E(c)$ lies in $[b_-(c),b_+(c)]$. If $c$ is in state $e$ and satisfies $C$'s precondition for parameter $i$, then $E(c)$ is in state $\rho(e)$, and it satisfies the precondition of the lockstep contract built from $C$ and $L$ at parameter $(i,c)$.
